gloss: not at all; not in the least (with negative)

definitions.gloss: not at all; not in the least; not a bit (with negative)
definitions.explanation: Used with a negative predicate to emphasize that something has not changed, improved, or happened at all. Expresses frustration or strong negation about the lack of progress or change.

examples.japanese: {一向|いっこう}に{構|かま}わない。
{雨|あめ}が{一向|いっこう}に{止|や}まない。
examples.english: The rain won't stop at all.

examples.japanese: {何度|なんど}{電話|でんわ}しても{一向|いっこう}につながらなくて{困|こま}っている。
examples.english: No matter how many times I call, it won't connect at all, and I'm at a loss.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always used with negative predicates (ない, ません, etc.). Expresses that a situation has not changed despite expectation or effort. Conveys a sense of frustration or emphasis. The exception is the fixed expression {一向|いっこう}に{構|かま}わない (I don't mind at all), which uses a negative verb but has an accepting nuance.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一向|いっこう}に{構|かま}わない (don't mind at all)
- {一向|いっこう}に{変|か}わらない (hasn't changed at all)
- {一向|いっこう}に{進|すす}まない (isn't progressing at all)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {全然|ぜんぜん}: not at all — more casual and versatile; can also be used with positive predicates in colloquial speech
- {少|すこ}しも: not even a little — similar emphasis on complete negation
